title: A Hell of a Shift
subtitle: Point-and-Click | Work Simulator | Puzzles | Game Studio
content: Point-and-Click | Work Simulator | Puzzles | Game Studio
summary: Implemented UI, dialogue, event, data, and drag-and-drop systems for a point-and-click studio sim.
description: A 2D point-and-click narrative puzzle game made in Unity and C#. Players take the role of a new game studio intern, complete tasks to progress their career, and manage a pressure gauge to avoid getting fired.

highlights.name: Pressure System
highlights.detail: The health system of the game which is affected by your ability to solve tasks and their accuracy.

highlights.name: Drag and Drop
highlights.detail: Main mechanic used in all puzzles of the game.

highlights.name: Complex UI System
highlights.detail: An entire complex system of UI screens working in sync across various systems.

highlights.name: Dialogue System
highlights.detail: A branching dialogue system presented through an in-game email interface.

highlights.name: Advanced Event Bus
highlights.detail: An event bus that fires different event types from specific trigger points in the game.

highlights.name: Data Handling
highlights.detail: A ScriptableObject data layer for characters, dialogue, tasks, events, and puzzles.

roles: Core Programmer and Producer in a team of 4
Collaborated on game system design as both programmer and producer
Implemented all core systems: UI, dialogue, event bus, drag-and-drop mechanics, and data management
Managed the JIRA board for task planning and team coordination
details: The player's objective is to grow from intern to full-time developer by completing tasks accurately and on time. Promotions introduce more responsibility, more complex tasks, and a rising pressure gauge. Beneath the workplace story is a darker secondary narrative: the studio setting and writing slowly reveal that career progress has a supernatural cost. I worked as core programmer and producer, implementing the main UI, dialogue, event, puzzle, and data systems while coordinating production tasks through JIRA.
